mentions.name: Configurable basement virtual space
mentions.description: A home basement conversion into a configurable virtual space using cheap projectors, lighting effects clamped to exposed ceiling joists like a truss, and furniture on wheels, combining full wall projections with sound and coordinated lighting. The author plans a network-coordinated camera/light platform built from a cheap projector, a Raspberry Pi, and directional LED lighting. The space doubles as an office, library, and game room, with ideas to use it to augment D&D games.
mentions.problem: The basement's white painted concrete floor is too bright, too cold, too hard, and too loud and needs to be replaced.
mentions.audience: The author's own household use; the basement also serves as a personal office, library, and game room.
mentions.source_excerpt: I’m experimenting with cheap projectors and lighting effects (using clamps to attach to the joists as if they were a truss) and furniture on wheels to create a configurable virtual space with full wall projections, sound, and lighting to match (but not overpower) the video. My plan is to make a camera/light platform with a cheap projector, and Raspberry Pi, and directional LED lighting so that I can coordinate all of them over the network.
